findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no (and any maximum-scale restriction) from the viewport meta tag so users can zoom.
findings.violation: user-scalable=no disables pinch to zoom, which prevents low vision users from magnifying the page and violates the expectation that users can resize text.

findings.evidence: Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk...
findings.fix: Change the inline color to #767676 or darker, or remove the color override so the default text color applies.
findings.violation: The text color #999999 against the page's default white background gives a contrast ratio of about 2.85 to 1, well under the 4.5 to 1 minimum for normal body text.

findings.fix: Add a caption element as the table's first child, for example "Zone status".
findings.violation: The table has no caption element, so a screen reader user who jumps directly to the table gets no description of what the Zone and Status columns represent.

findings.fix: Replace the fixed width with a responsive rule such as max-width:960px; width:100%.
findings.violation: A fixed 960px width does not adapt to the mobile viewport the page itself declares (width=device-width), which forces horizontal scrolling on narrow screens.

findings.fix: Remove the fixed height and overflow:hidden, or replace height with min-height so the box can grow with its content.
findings.violation: The fixed 60px height combined with overflow:hidden will clip the paragraph text inside it whenever the user increases text size or zooms, hiding part of the message.

findings.evidence: <button type="button" class="btn-secondary" id="s3-button1" style="border:1px solid #9d9d9d">Refresh status</button>
findings.fix: Darken the border color to at least #767676 so it reaches 3 to 1 contrast against the background.
findings.violation: The #9d9d9d border against the page's white background gives a contrast ratio of about 2.7 to 1, below the 3 to 1 minimum needed for a visible UI component boundary.

findings.evidence: Choose a plan
findings.fix: Mark the steps up as an ordered list with li elements, and add aria-current="step" to the active step.
findings.violation: The three sequential steps are plain divs with no list markup and no indication of which step is current, so a screen reader user cannot tell this is an ordered sequence or where they are in it.

findings.evidence: read the accessibility improvements list
findings.fix: Reword the link text to describe where it actually goes, for example "read the list of upcoming fare adjustments".
findings.location: section "Weekend service", link in the paragraph after the wizard (id s3-link1)
findings.violation: The link text says "read the accessibility improvements list" but the href points to /fares/history, so the visible label does not match the destination, which misleads anyone scanning link text or a screen reader's links list.

findings.fix: Change the label's for attribute to "topic" so it matches the select element's id.
findings.location: section "Weekend service", form Route field (label id s3-form-topic-label and select id topic)
findings.violation: The label's for attribute references "topic-alt", which does not match any element id on the page, so the label is not programmatically associated with the select and a screen reader will not announce "Route" when the field receives focus.

findings.evidence: Enter a 6 character code using letters and numbers only.
findings.location: section "Weekend service", form promo code field (input id promo and error span id s3-form-promo-error)
findings.violation: The input is marked aria-invalid="true" but has no aria-describedby pointing at the adjacent error message, so a screen reader announces that the field is invalid without ever reading why.
